title: Efficient and precise programmable DNA knock-in without double-strand breaks.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the Figshare deposit via its application programming interface: 18 raw FASTQ (compressed sequencing read) files, 996 MB total, CC BY 4.0, covering only 3 genomic sites (ACTB, TRAC, HEK4). Downloaded and opened all 14 source-data spreadsheets from github.com/WangHFlab/KNIT plus the two identical Nature supplementary spreadsheets: 448 KB total, 71 figure-panel sheets, 395 non-empty rows, 2,089 numeric cells, no column headers in machine-readable form.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The abstract's claims (0.7 kb to >10 kb inserts, up to 89% efficiency, CAR-T results). The article full text is paywalled and absent from PubMed Central, so I could not read Methods; the 14 MB Supplementary Information PDF (which likely holds guide RNA and donor sequence tables) was found but not parsed, because the spreadsheets had already settled the verdict.

a1_downloadable.note: Verified: Figshare deposit is public CC BY 4.0 and the GitHub source-data spreadsheets downloaded without any login. No access application needed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: KILLER. No feature/label table exists anywhere. The knock-in efficiency values live as bare bar-chart numbers in 71 differently-shaped figure panels with merged, hand-written condition headers ('sgNT', 'KE1', '5.6k'); a modellable label column would have to be reconstructed panel by panel. The alternative route, deriving efficiencies from the deposited FASTQ files, means running an amplicon-analysis pipeline first, i.e. constructing the label from raw reads.

a3_inputs_present.note: Verified absent: the spreadsheets contain no guide RNA sequences, donor-template sequences, homology-arm lengths or genomic coordinates. Only short condition names. Any input features would have to be hand-transcribed from a 14 MB supplementary PDF.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are implied, never stated in a column. The same sheets mix percent-of-cells by flow cytometry, fold-change by quantitative PCR, percent viability, and translocation frequencies near 0.0001, with nothing marking which is which except the figure caption in the paywalled paper.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified by counting: 395 non-empty rows and 2,089 numeric cells across all 14 files, and those are replicate measurements of ~70 unrelated experiments. The modelling unit (locus x donor design x cell type) numbers a few dozen at most, across roughly a dozen loci. Checklist threshold is ~1,500 labelled rows.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.45 GB (448 KB spreadsheets; 996 MB FASTQ if ever needed)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is the one thing that is not a problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing contradicts: the two Nature supplementary spreadsheets are byte-identical in size to GitHub's Source Data Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 (21,537 and 43,436 bytes), so the two distribution routes agree.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is genuinely physical, which is the one strength: the numbers are flow cytometry, droplet digital PCR and amplicon sequencing measurements made in the lab, not another model's output. This does not rescue A2, A3, A4 or A5.

existing_models.name: CRISPRon (guide RNA on-target cutting efficiency predictor)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not assessed; retrieved only as a search result describing training on 23,902 guide RNAs. It predicts cutting, not kilobase knock-in.

existing_models.name: Random-forest predictor of homology-directed repair efficiency (Scientific Reports 2019, nature.com/articles/s41598-019-39142-0)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not assessed; search snippet reports an 83% improvement in homology-directed repair efficiency over conventionally chosen targets. It covers short single-stranded oligonucleotide edits, not kilobase inserts.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: the deposited files carry no sequence, coordinate or standard identifier to join on.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: with roughly a dozen genomic sites and no recorded design features, any model would be describing a handful of hand-picked experiments rather than predicting anything.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use target-site and donor-template design features to predict how efficiently a large DNA cassette is inserted at that site.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on each (genomic target site, guide RNA, donor-template design, cell type) combination tested. Verified count: roughly a dozen distinct loci and a few dozen condition combinations, far short of what training needs.
plain_idea.predict: Percent of cells carrying the correct kilobase-scale insertion, measured by flow cytometry for fluorescent-protein cassettes and by amplicon sequencing for sequence-level outcomes.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Gene-therapy and CAR-T (chimeric antigen receptor T cell) groups currently pick insertion sites by trial and error, so a site-ranking model would save months of wet-lab work. This paper simply does not contain enough sites to build one.

ml_idea: Rejected idea: predict kilobase-scale knock-in efficiency from target-site sequence, guide RNA and donor-template design, so that gene-therapy groups could rank candidate insertion sites before doing any wet-lab work. The data to support it is not here. The useful observation for the scout pipeline is that this is a textbook example of a high-profile method paper whose deposited data is 996 MB of raw reads from 3 sites plus bar-chart source data, which is correct and complete practice for a tool paper and completely unusable for machine learning.

effort.compute_note: Measured file sizes directly (448 KB of spreadsheets, 996 MB of FASTQ listed by the Figshare API). No modelling time estimated because no feature table can be built.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the source-data spreadsheets and count rows. It took one script: 395 non-empty rows across 71 figure panels, which kills the project in under five minutes.

verdict_reason: A CRISPR method paper, not a dataset paper. All deposited data is either raw sequencing reads from three genomic sites or bar-chart figure source data; there is no feature/label table, no guide or donor sequences, no units column, and only ~395 rows across ~a dozen loci. Fails A2, A3, A4 and A5.
